item.title: Mount Ontake: A Sacred Volcanic Mountain of Pilgrimage — Guide
item.description: Mount Ontake is Japan’s second-highest volcano at 3,067 metres, straddling the border of Gifu and Nagano, and has been revered as a sacred mountain for centuries, serving as a major centre of the shugendo and Ontake-kyo mountain-worship traditions with shrines, stone monuments and pilgrim trails on its slopes. The mountain offers dramatic high-altitude volcanic scenery and hiking, though it is an active volcano; following an eruption in 2014, access to certain areas near the summit has at times been restricted, so current conditions and any restrictions should always be checked before planning to climb.
